name: South Dublin County Council
request_description:
I am writing to submit an application under the provisions of the Freedom of Information Act, 2014. 

My request pertains to certain records related to Approved Housing Bodies (AHBs) and their vacant units in your Council area. 

I would greatly appreciate your assistance in providing the following information.

In response to a recent press query seeking specific data on Approved Housing Bodies, I was informed by the Council’s communications department that there in 2023, there were 16 AHB units that “fall under various categories such as hard to let, works required, legal issues etc.”

With regard to those 16 vacant units, I am hereby requesting the following records:

a. A comprehensive list of the aforementioned units, including their respective addresses and the names of the AHBs responsible for owning/managing each of these units, and the length of time these units have remained vacant as of January 2023.

Please note:

I would like to bring to your attention the 2015 Value-for-Money report on Approved Housing Bodies issued by the Local Government Auditor. 

The report emphasizes the necessity for local authorities to maintain a management information system encompassing details of all properties provided by AHBs, whether purchased, built, or leased units. 

It states:

“The local authorities need to operate a management information system which maintains
details of all properties provided by the AHBs (whether purchased/built or leased units), and
should be agreed periodically with the Department. Details of the tenants of each property,
nomination details, and rent scheme details should also be maintained. The system should
also track details of voids, length of time for re-lets, details of property inspections etc.”

Given this recommendation, I assume that the Council has access to the requested information through its property management system, rendering it eligible for release under section 17(4) of the FOI Act. 

This section mandates FOI bodies to undertake reasonable efforts to search for and extract data, even if a new record is not created.

b. I am also requesting copies of the Annual Statements of Occupancy for each vacant unit covering the years 2020, 2021, and 2022.

Please note: The 2015 Value-for-Money report states that AHBs should submit annual statements of occupancy to the local authorities for all properties funded by the latter. 

The report states:

“It is recommended that an annual statement of occupancy should be submitted by the AHBs to the local authority for all properties funded by the local authorities.”


c. Finally, I seek access to any communications exchanged between the AHBs responsible for owning/managing the aforementioned vacant units, and your Council's Housing Section, that pertain to the vacant units. 

The timeframe I am referring to for these communications is from 2020 to the present.

I kindly request that the information be made available in electronic format.

request_description: Re: Crooksling Nursing Home, Blessington Road, N81, Dublin 24 We refer to the above-named site/area and we note that this site is owned by the HSE  and the HSE offered the property to all State Stakeholders through the Intra-State  Property Register and the Department of Children, Equality, Disability, Integration and Youth expressed an interest in Crooksling to facilitate the provisions of suitable accommodation to persons seeking international protection. We would be grateful for a full copy of the planning files/licenses for the property to  be used as an international protection center. We seek this information under the Freedom of Information Act and Planning Acts.  We would also be grateful for a copy of the grant of permission for this site to be used for tented accommodation. We act on behalf of clients who have concerns in relation to this site being used for the above accommodation due to the rural location, lack of facilities, breach of planning  regulations, which would extend to proposed water, surface water and foul drainage system. Without proper planning this would cause a real risk and concern to the local area. This site is located in an area zoned Objective RU in the South Dublin County  Council Development Plan 2000-2028, which seeks 'to protect and improve Rural  Amenity and to provide for the development of Agriculture. Therefore we would propose this development would materially contravene the objectives of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan, particularly that of Policy H16 and would lead to demands for the uneconomic provision of further public services and facilities Pg. 1 in this rural area. The proposed development would  therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.There is a significant increase in traffic and this will also lead to additional demand for access to services in an area that has no services to offer. The public road has no footpaths, there are no public lighting between the site and the closest town and is not safe for pedestrian access, there is poor vertical and horizontal alignment, lacks pedestrian, public lighting. We submit on behalf of our clients that this site is being used without permission and in breach of the planning acts and the Development plan. This development, by reason of its scale, design, mass and bulk, fails to respond to the site's sensitive context, it is visually incongruous to the rural area and would lead to the loss of rural amenity which materially contravenes Policy H23 Rural House and Extension Design Objective 1 and the RU zoning objective and would be contrary to the provisions of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2022-2028. We further submit this site has now caused serious public safety by reason of traffic and therefore is contrary to the proper planning and sustainability development in the area Our client has also brought to our attention that there are previous planning applications Our client has also brought to our attention that there are previous planning applications in this local area that have all since been refused for once off planning permission due We believe this accommodation center for international applicants does not have the proper planning to operate and therefore we ask that you furnish us with a copy of the planning permission for the site. We would ask you to provide how many people are living on this site and how the waste is being managed and send us any reports or screening you have done or are in your possession regarding same.
